claims.text: PE: apixaban, rivaroxaban and edoxaban can be used for both initial and maintenance therapy;
claims.quote: The oral factor Xa inhibitor anticoagulants apixaban, edoxaban, and rivaroxaban can be used for both initial and maintenance anticoagulation therapy
were as effective (in non-inferiority analyses) as warfarin in preventing recurrent DVT and PE
rates of major bleeding, including intracranial hemorrhage, were significantly lower with oral factor Xa inhibitor anticoagulants than with warfarin

claims.text: Rivaroxaban and apixaban need no parenteral lead-in; edoxaban needs 5–10 days of a parenteral anticoagulant.
claims.quote: Although rivaroxaban and apixaban do not require overlap with a parenteral anticoagulant when used as initial therapy, edoxaban requires use of a parenteral anticoagulant for 5 to 10 days.
Duration of maintenance anticoagulation for PE is dependent on a variety of factors (eg, risk factors for PE, bleeding risk) and can range from 3 months to lifelong therapy.

claims.text: 3 months for a clearly transient risk factor (immobilization, recent surgery, trauma).
claims.quote: Clearly transient risk factors (eg, immobilization, recent surgery, trauma) require only 3 months of treatment.

claims.text: Azole antifungals and protease inhibitors raise oral Xa inhibitor levels; certain antiseizure drugs and rifampin lower them.
claims.quote: azole antifungal therapy and protease inhibitors will increase oral factor Xa inhibitor levels, and certain antiseizure medications and rifampin will decrease oral factor Xa inhibitor levels
